```sql
WITH totals AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
           count(*)           AS order_count,
           max(o.created_at)  AS last_order_at
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
       AND o.customer_id IN (
             SELECT c2.id
               FROM customers c2
              WHERE c2.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
           )
     GROUP BY o.customer_id
    HAVING count(o.created_at) = count(*)
       AND max(o.created_at) >= %(from)s
       AND max(o.created_at) <  %(to)s
)
SELECT c.id,
       c.email,
       c.company,
       c.country_code,
       t.revenue,
       t.order_count,
       t.last_order_at
  FROM customers c
  JOIN totals t ON t.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
 ORDER BY t.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De query scant `orders` nu één keer, beperkt tot klanten van de tenant, in plaats van de hele tabel te materialiseren en twee keer te verwerken (aggregatie plus `DISTINCT ON` met sort). `max(created_at)` vervangt de `DISTINCT ON`; de `count(created_at) = count(*)`-check behoudt het originele gedrag als `created_at` NULL kan zijn, want dan was `last_order_at` NULL en viel de klant af. Het venstervoorwaarde filtert vóór de join en `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` blijven ongewijzigd.
